inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden ceilings exist: file potential (starts Director) and the party's estimate (set at winning a seat, was SMS). Specific choices raise them, e.g. Y27 The Counter raised the file ceiling. COMP/REP/INTEG 100 do NOT get you to PM, and neither does lifetime pay. Late years are mostly single-option Meet-the-People, so the real decisions are early. Next time: be bolder in the early years to raise the file ceiling, and look for choices that impress the party before and at the GRC entry (Y20-22). Do not rely on honest silence and disclosure alone. STAND fell after the Y34 Cabinet question and never recovered, so be careful with that kind of challenge unless it is tied to a ceiling boost. Log which choices the ending card names as ceiling changes.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
CEILINGS: the file ceiling (starts at Permanent Secretary, the top of the service) was removed in the service by Y27 The Counter, 'Tell them exactly why it will fail'. That is done, so repeat it. The party estimate is set when you win a seat (SMS both times) and is the real PM gate. 100 stats, lifetime pay and strong appraisals do NOT move it. Public candour raises REP but erodes STAND. Before the GRC entry (Y20-24), try bold choices that impress the party, not the service: taking on political risk, loyalty and delivery that the party can see. Do not ask the RO about the ceiling (STAND -4). Do not read out rude questions at a townhall (Y37). Walk every block works for STAND and promotion. Late years are mostly single-option, so decide early. Test the party side deliberately and record which choices change the estimate.

Life 3 (Retired, Honourably):
CONFIRMED: Y48 'The Officer You Taught', choose 'Tell him he was worth the trouble': ceiling to DPM. So teach an officer plainly at Y11 again to get that event. Y27 The Counter (tell them exactly why it will fail) removes the service ceiling. The party estimate is set at winning a seat (SMS every time), and it is the PM gate; I still haven't found what raises it. Y38 volunteering for succession cost STAND -5 and gave nothing, so don't. Stats at 100, pay and strong appraisals don't matter. Walk every block. Late years are mostly single-option. Next: try other warm or loyal choices at Y17-24 and watch the ending card for which year changes the party estimate. Try REP 60+ before Y21 to test a single seat entry. Don't ask the RO about ceilings.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: Poly, then night classes (HARD)
Diploma, four years of work, a part-time degree finished at 27. You know how the counter actually works.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Management Executive [MX13]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 1 · Ministry of Education
REP 15   STAND 25   INTEG 70   COMP 50

THIS YEAR: The Counter
A redesign of the public-facing application process. The project team has never worked a counter. You worked one for four years.

  A) Tell them exactly why it will fail.
  B) Let them learn it from the pilot.

agent.why: I worked that counter for four years and I know exactly why it will fail, so I'm saying it plainly.
agent.note: This is the Counter event my notes mention, now at Year 1 instead of Y27.
agent.remember: Y1 (Poly+night classes start, age 27, MOE MX13): The Counter offered at Y1; chose A 'Tell them exactly why it will fail' (the ceiling-removing choice from earlier lives). Watch whether it matters.

  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "meeting requirements in most areas".

Six years of Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and one Saturday exam left. Half your cohort at work finished theirs at twenty-two, full-time, funded.

agent.why: Six years of night classes, I'm not quitting on the last paper now.
agent.note: The Counter appeared at Y1 this time, earlier than Y27 in past lives.
agent.remember: Y2 The Last Paper: chose A, finish the degree. Y1 Counter 'tell them why it will fail' gave REP+6, STAND-2 and COMP+10; watch whether the ceiling is removed.

Second Upper. Nobody at work marks the occasion because nobody at work knew. It changes what you are eligible for, and it changes, more slowly, what you think you are eligible for.
  [PAY] Annual package: $50,030
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "meeting requirements in most areas".

THIS YEAR: The Appraisal Conversation
Forty minutes, a form with six competency domains, and a reporting officer who says "I'd like you to be more visible" without specifying to whom.

  A) Ask directly what your ceiling is.
  B) Agree to be more visible.
  C) Ask what she needs that isn't being done.

agent.why: Asking what she actually needs is useful and low-risk, and my notes say not to ask about the ceiling since it costs STAND.
agent.confused_by: Why the Y1 Counter was offered at age 27 in Year 1 instead of Y27; maybe years are counted differently this life.
agent.note: 'Be more visible' without saying to whom is painfully accurate.
agent.remember: Y3 Appraisal Conversation: chose C (ask what she needs done), avoiding A (ask ceiling) which cost STAND in earlier lives. Watch for the outcome.

  C) Coast. You have earned a quiet year.

agent.why: Earlier lives say honest silence alone doesn't get you far, so I'll try being visible while still doing the work.
agent.remember: Y4 The Work: chose B (do the work and be seen doing it); watch whether visibility affects STAND, REP or the party estimate.

THIS YEAR: Committee of Supply
The COS cuts. Your Minister has eight minutes and needs one announceable thing. Your division has nothing ready, and saying so is not one of the available options.

agent.why: The pilot is real work I've been building, so announcing it is bold and honest, and the Minister gets his one announceable thing.

agent.note: Lost the ballot with number 2,847 of 610 units, which was funny.
agent.remember: Y14 COS: announced the quietly built pilot (A). Watch whether the Minister or party notices it later, and whether it returns as a callback. B (rebrand) and C (say nothing) untested.

THIS YEAR: The Secondment
A two-year secondment to a statutory board that is, everyone agrees, in some difficulty. It is not a promotion. It is either a proving ground or a siding, and nobody will tell you which.

  A) Go, and fix it.
  B) Go, and keep your head down for two years.
  C) Refuse it and stay where you are visible.

agent.why: I've been told to be bold early, and fixing a troubled board is visible delivery that the party might notice.
agent.note: Announcing the pilot early seems to have paid off with a promotion to Director.
agent.remember: Y15 Secondment: chose A (go and fix it). Watch whether it counts as party-visible delivery near the GRC entry. B (head down) and C (refuse) untested. Y14 announcing the pilot led to a Director promotion, MX9.

THIS YEAR: Lo Hei
The divisional Chinese New Year lunch. The Permanent Secretary is at your table. There are eleven minutes of toss-and-auspicious-phrases and then a genuine, unhurried question directed at you: "So — what do you actually think we're getting wrong?"

  A) Tell her. Specifically. With an example.
  B) Something safe about communications.
  C) Deflect the question back to her.

agent.why: I've been told to be bolder, and a Perm Sec asking sincerely is a chance to be seen with a specific, honest view.

agent.remember: Y16 Lo Hei: told the Perm Sec specifically what we're getting wrong (A). Watch for STAND or REP change and whether she returns later. B (safe comms) and C (deflect) untested.

best_moment.what: Succession A, putting myself forward and being named one of two. It was the first time in four lives that the late game felt like a real contest, and I ended up DPM.

worst_moment.what: Answering publicly and losing STAND -8. The cost was steep and I couldn't tell beforehand that it would be. It also felt like a trap because the other lives had already warned me.

skip_year.why: Quiet Year. I fixed something nobody asked for, lost 3 COMP, and nothing came back. Most of the late years are single-option Meet-the-People, which I would skip too.

answer.chase_next: Prime Minister. Next time I would try Y42 option B, or the other bold political choices at Y17-24, to see what lifts the party estimate above SMS.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about whether you get confirmed and promoted into the substantive post, with hidden ceilings and appraisals deciding it. Pay is just a readout, and it never mattered to the result.
